Let
\[
A_n=\int_{[0,1]^4}e^{-n(P^2+Q^2)}\,d\mathbf x,\qquad B_n=I_n(0).
\]
Then
\[
I_n(\lambda)=A_n\sinh\lambda+B_n,
\]
so the unique root satisfies
\[
\sinh\lambda_n=-\frac{B_n}{A_n}.
\]

First,
\[
\int_{[0,1]^2} e^{-n(xy)^2}\,dx\,dy
=\int_0^1 e^{-np^2}(-\log p)\,dp.
\]
With \(p=z/\sqrt n\),
\[
\int_0^1 e^{-np^2}(-\log p)\,dp
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\int_0^{\sqrt n}e^{-z^2}\left(\frac12\log n-\log z\right)\,dz
\sim \frac{\sqrt\pi}{4\sqrt n}\log n.
\]
Hence
\[
A_n\sim \frac{\pi}{16n}(\log n)^2.
\]

Now compute \(B_n\). For each \((j,k)\), set
\[
P=\delta 2^{-j}u,\qquad Q=\delta 2^{-k}v.
\]
The product-density identity gives
\[
d\mathbf x=(-\log P)(-\log Q)\,dP\,dQ.
\]
The \(j,k\)-sum collapses because
\[
\sum_{j,k=0}^1(-1)^{j+k}
\bigl(-\log(\delta2^{-j}u)\bigr)
\bigl(-\log(\delta2^{-k}v)\bigr)
=(\log2)^2.
\]
Thus
\[
B_n=\delta^2(\log2)^2\sum_{t=0}^2(-1)^t\binom2t J_t+o(\cdots),
\]
where
\[
J_t=\int_{u,v\ge0}G_t(u,v)\,du\,dv.
\]

Use
\[
r=uv,\qquad s=(u-v)^2.
\]
The map \((u,v)\mapsto(r,s)\) is two-to-one away from \(u=v\), and
\[
\left|\frac{\partial(r,s)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|
=2|u^2-v^2|.
\]
Therefore
\[
J_t=-2N e^{-4N}
\int_{r,s\ge0}
(r+s+1)\left(r+s-1-\frac{\delta^2}{4}\right)(r-s+\delta^3)
e^{-N((r-a_t)^2+(s-b_t)^2)}\,dr\,ds.
\]

The full-plane Gaussian integral vanishes, since after writing
\[
r=a_t+x,\qquad s=b_t+y,
\]
we have \(r-s+\delta^3=x-y\), while the remaining factor depends only on \(x+y\). Thus only the two boundary tails \(r<0\) and \(s<0\) contribute.

Put \(N=\delta^{-2}\). A one-sided Gaussian tail expansion gives
\[
\sum_{t=0}^2(-1)^t\binom2t J_t
\sim 12\sqrt\pi\,N^{-3}e^{-5N}.
\]
Hence
\[
B_n\sim
\delta^2(\log2)^2\cdot 12\sqrt\pi\,N^{-3}e^{-5N}
=12\sqrt\pi(\log2)^2N^{-4}e^{-5N}.
\]
Since \(N=\sqrt n\),
\[
B_n\sim 12\sqrt\pi(\log2)^2n^{-2}e^{-5\sqrt n}.
\]

Therefore
\[
\lambda_n\sim-\frac{B_n}{A_n}
\sim
-\frac{12\sqrt\pi(\log2)^2n^{-2}e^{-5\sqrt n}}
{\frac{\pi}{16n}(\log n)^2}
=
-\frac{192(\log2)^2}{\sqrt\pi}\,
\frac{e^{-5\sqrt n}}{n(\log n)^2}.
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{\alpha=1,\qquad \beta=2,\qquad c=5,\qquad L=-\frac{192(\log2)^2}{\sqrt\pi}}.
\]
